The failing test is `testReadingOfFirstStoredEntry()` which opens a zip file "COMPRESS-264.zip" and reads the first zip entry expecting a size of 5 and data "data\n". The test fails because with version 1.7 of commons-compress the content read is corrupted with NUL bytes, while 1.6 reads correctly.

The core method invoked is `ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry()`. This method reads the Local File Header (LFH) from the zip stream, processes entry metadata like method, size, name, extra fields, then sets up the input stream for reading compressed data. For the first entry, it calls `readFirstLocalFileHeader` which can detect split archives and adjusts accordingly.

The bug report shows 1.7 produces wrong data content (NUL bytes), while 1.6 works as expected. This suggests an issue in either reading or interpreting the LFH or subsequent data bytes.

Inspecting the `getNextZipEntry` snippet:

- It reads the LFH bytes into a buffer.
- Parses version, flags, compression method, sizes and file name.
- If no data descriptor, it reads CRC, compressed size, and uncompressed size directly.
- Calls `processZip64Extra` to adjust sizes if Zip64 extra fields are present.
- Sets up the compressed data input stream based on compression method.
- Returns the `ZipArchiveEntry` that was set up.

From the bug report and code snippet, the suspicious area is how compressed size and uncompressed size are parsed and handled.

Also relevant is the use of data descriptor flag. When data descriptor is used (the sizes are not in LFH), reading compressed data and setting the size depends on reading the data descriptor after the compressed data.

The test is verifying the first stored entry that is 5 bytes of uncompressed data. A stored entry means no compression (method 0).

Potential reasons for the bug:

- The compressed size or size fields are read incorrectly from the LFH or extra fields in 1.7.
- The input stream for reading the entry data is not properly set for stored entries.
- The sizes are not properly set or updated due to missing or incorrect handling of data descriptor.
- Changes in 1.7 (vs 1.6) may have altered the logic to handle stored entries or data descriptors causing corruption.

The recent bug reports are unrelated (7z and classic UNIX compress).

No obvious errors surfaced from `closeEntry` which drains or skips remaining bytes.

Therefore likely the root cause is that in `getNextZipEntry`, the implementation in 1.7 mishandles the sizes or input stream setup for stored entries (non-compressed method), especially when data descriptor is or is not used, leading to reading incorrect bytes (zeroed or uninitialized bytes).

This matches the symptoms of garbage/NUL bytes read for data content at test read.

# Diagnosis
The bug is caused by incorrect handling of the size and input stream setup for stored (non-compressed) ZIP entries when reading the local file header and initializing the entry input stream in `ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry()`. The change from commons-compress 1.6 to 1.7 introduced an erroneous handling of compressed size or data descriptor flags that results in reading incorrect bytes (NULs) instead of the actual entry data, making the test fail with modified content. The fault likely lies in how the compressed size is extracted or how the input stream is created for stored entries with or without data descriptors.

The method `ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry()` is the best place to fix this, potentially also involving size related calculations in `processZip64Extra(size, cSize)` or the input stream construction based on entry method.

Suggested locations to fix:
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry()

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
